findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda environment variable block, committed to source control and visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the state file.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy, and no client-side encryption is used.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unaddressed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network segmentation controls, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.

The assume role policy allows the entire lambda.amazonaws.com service principal to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, permitting cross-account confused-deputy abuse of the role.
